publicComments.name: Johanna Mora
publicComments.summary: Asked the board to consider bringing middle school back to elementary school campuses citing family convenience, cost savings, safety, and enrollment benefits.

publicComments.name: Yesenia Soriano (Jessica Soriano, translated)
publicComments.summary: A parent of an Orion preschool student asked the board not to close the Orion preschool program, citing its importance to her and the community.

publicComments.name: Lucely Enriquez (translated)
publicComments.summary: A parent described her son's progress at Orion's preschool program due to his autism and asked the board to keep preschool at Orion for the Latino community.

publicComments.name: Nancy Espinoza
publicComments.summary: As lead teacher at Orion preschool, she described facility and relocation issues over the past year and asked the board to keep the preschool program at Orion.

publicComments.name: Steve Yike
publicComments.summary: As Orion School Site Council chair, he asked the board to fund a full-time office assistant position at Orion given increased enrollment and office workload.

publicComments.name: Valentina Chinchilla
publicComments.summary: A 4th grade student at Orion shared her personal connection to the preschool program (her mother teaches there) and asked the board to keep it at Orion.

publicComments.name: John Chow
publicComments.summary: Representing Schools Beyond Screens, he raised concerns about a gap between district messaging on screen use and classroom reality, and voiced support for the Tech Advisory Committee.

publicComments.name: Megan (on behalf of Tyrell Day)
publicComments.summary: A parent voiced support for reopening the Orion preschool/Spanish immersion program at its original campus rather than Roosevelt.

publicComments.name: Shawna Ingersoll
publicComments.summary: CSEA labor representative congratulated the outgoing board president and thanked the board for considering the CSEA agreement.

Approval of Board Policy 6163.4: Student Use of Technology
Approval of Intentional Technology for Empowered Learning Committee

publicComments.name: Serena Facchinetti
publicComments.summary: Supported forming the committee but urged ongoing monitoring of technology changes and immediate guardrails, especially a moratorium on generative AI in K-8 classrooms.

publicComments.name: Michelle Strope
publicComments.summary: Raised concerns about excessive screen time for young children and urged district-wide guidance and equity considerations around technology requirements.

publicComments.name: Chris Terry
publicComments.summary: Described concerns about teachers using screens in place of direct instruction and screens being used as rewards, while supporting the new technology committee.

publicComments.name: Jackie Selby
publicComments.summary: Asked for increased transparency around corporate donations and edtech partnerships/vendor deals in schools.

publicComments.name: Alexis D'Agostino
publicComments.summary: Shared an anecdote about her daughter seeing a YouTube ad in class and asked for immediate low-cost fixes like disabling ads via Google Classroom settings.

publicComments.name: Xiao Yang
publicComments.summary: Raised data privacy concerns about third-party educational apps collecting student data without clear policies or parental consent.

publicComments.name: Emily Khan
publicComments.summary: Shared experience with inconsistent screen use practices across TK classrooms and expressed support for district-wide technology policy.

publicComments.name: Daniel
publicComments.summary: Questioned the evidence base and data privacy practices for educational apps like i-Ready and Raz Plus used in the Mandarin immersion program.

publicComments.name: Phil Luna
publicComments.summary: Thanked the board and superintendent, and raised questions about committee updates, opt-out options, and cost analysis for the technology initiative.
